blocks.text:
After breakfast, take a sightseeing tour of Antigua.

You will see the ruins, museums, monasteries, markets, art galleries and squares of the colonial city.

Visit Parque Central and the Cathedral of San José, the Palace of the Captains General dating from 1558, the municipal building constructed in 1740, the ruins of Las Capuchinas convent and the Santa Catalina Arch.

Another stop is La Merced Church, with its carved façade. The programme also includes the ruins of the San Jerónimo religious school, dating from 1739. Classical music concerts are held here among the gardens and surviving walls.

The city is also home to San Francisco Church, one of Antigua’s oldest churches, the restored colonial mansion Casa Popenoe, the Museo de Santiago in the former prison, the Museo del Libro Antiguo and the Museum of Colonial Art in the former university building.

You will see Parque de la Unión, with its open-air textile market, San Pedro Church and the former Santa Clara convent.

In the afternoon, transfer to Panajachel. The drive takes about 1 hour.

blocks.text:
In the morning, take a boat trip on Lake Atitlán. The crossing takes about 30 minutes.

This morning, you will take a boat tour of the "place where the rainbow finds its colors," which is the translation of Lake Atitlán. The lake is located in central Guatemala, covering an area of over 130 square kilometers, with a depth of 340 meters, making it the deepest lake in Central America. Surrounding it are mountains and 3 volcanoes: San Pedro, Atitlán, and Tolimán. Ash from these volcanoes created the uneven landscape, giving rise to the lake at an altitude of 1560 meters above sea level. Since 1955, the area around Atitlán has been considered a national park.

Along the shores, local Mayan tribes live. They still preserve their traditions, speak their native language, and wear traditional clothing. You will also visit the village of San Juan La Laguna, where you can visit a women's textile cooperative and see hand-weaving and the natural dyeing process.

Next, you'll visit the workshops of local naïve artists, and the tour will continue to the town of Santiago.

In the evening, transfer to Guatemala City.
